newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Ireland, Portugal welcome lira back to ERM.
newsitem.headline: Ireland, Portugal welcome lira back to ERM.

text.p: The prime ministers of Ireland and Portugal welcomed news Italy had re-joined the European exchange rate mechanism (ERM) which they said would contribute to stability and build confidence in the European single currency.

"I think it is a good sign that the number of countries likely to be taking part in the first wave of membership of the European currency would be larger than might have been anticipated a year or so ago," said Irish Prime Minister John Bruton.

"This builds confidence in the Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) project," he told a news conference during a brief visit to Lisbon to prepare for a European Union (EU) summit in Dublin on December 13-14.
Prime Minister Antonio Guterres said: "Anything that contributes to monetary stability at a European level is positive. We welcome the entry of the lira to the ERM."
He added "We want the biggest possible number of countries to give dimension and force to the European single currency."

Two days of hard bargaining in Brussels culminated late on Sunday night in an agreement by EU finance ministers and central bank governors to let the lira rejoin the ERM at a central rate of 990 lira to the mark.
